title: 3.3 Derivatives of the Inverse Trigonometric Functions

icans: I can find the derivative of an inverse function at a point using g′(b) = 1/f′(a).
I can find the derivatives of sin⁻¹x, cos⁻¹x, and tan⁻¹x.
I can use the Chain Rule with inverse trig functions.

blocks.p: f(x) = x³ and g(x) = ∛x are inverses.

blocks.sec: Part 2 · Notes and examples (fill in each note, then work the example)

notes: Derivative of an inverse: if f(a) = b, then (f⁻¹)′(b) = _______________.

blocks.stem: f(x) = x³ + x + 1 and g = f⁻¹. Find g′(3).

notes: Inverse sine and cosine: d/dx sin⁻¹x = 1/√(1 − x²) and d/dx cos⁻¹x = _______________.

f(x) = tan⁻¹x. Find f′(√3) and f′(−1).

notes: Chain Rule: d/dx tan⁻¹u = u′/(1 + u²) and d/dx sin⁻¹u = _______________.
